chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Dirraj, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who freed his slave upon his death, while the slave had a debt, he said: 'If the value of the slave is equal to the debt and equal to it (i.e., covers it), the manumission is valid; otherwise, it is not valid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing a slave if the owner dies with debt?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chain of the Six Companions clarifies the priority of debt repayment over manumission in Shia jurisprudence, establishing that the slave's value must exceed the debt for the emancipation to be valid. It reflects the principle that the owner's discretionary gift (hibq) is suspended if it impairs the creditors' rights, ensuring financial obligations are settled before the slave's freedom is recognized.
